title: Fujitsu's Arm-based Monaka Data Center CPU at Hot Chips 2026
gist: Fujitsu detailed Monaka, a 144-core Armv9.3-A data center CPU arriving in 2027 with 256-bit SVE2 SIMDs, 3D-stacked TSMC N2P core dies over N5 SRAM and I/O dies, and 12 channels of DDR5. Its differentiating bet is running at roughly 30% lower voltage than comparable designs for energy efficiency, with sovereign AI as an explicit target and a 1.4nm Monaka-X with NVLink Fusion already in development.

insights.claim: Fujitsu says Monaka runs voltages around 30% lower than similar designs, though it is not disclosing the specific voltages, exploiting that power scales with the square of voltage.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: A 30% voltage reduction implies roughly halved dynamic power at equal frequency, the core claim to verify when silicon ships.
insights.quote: Fujitsu says that they are running the voltages at around 30% lower than similar designs, but they are not disclosing the specific voltages they are running at.
insights.locator: Thanks to one of the core rules of chip operation

insights.claim: Running at ultra-low voltages is a non-standard way of designing chips and required special design tools to accomplish.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Custom EDA flow is a real barrier to imitation, but also an execution risk that could delay or degrade the product.
insights.quote: There is a strong emphasis here on how this is a non-standard way of designing chips, and required special design tools to help accomplish it.
insights.locator: Thanks to one of the core rules of chip operation

insights.claim: Fujitsu gave low dropout regulators particular focus because they are analog circuits that do not shrink well with smaller process nodes, helping the design hit a better cost-versus-performance level.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Analog circuits that resist scaling are an underappreciated driver of chiplet partitioning decisions across the industry.
insights.locator: Fujitsu also gave low dropout regulators (LDOs) a particular focus

insights.claim: Monaka's value proposition is that AI adoption is currently constrained by power limitations, which the design addresses by running at ultra-low voltages for maximum efficiency.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Positions Monaka to win in power-capped data centers rather than on absolute performance, a different competitive lane from EPYC and Xeon.
insights.quote: Monaka’s value proposition is that AI adoption is currently constrained by power limitations, which Monaka addresses by running at ultra-low-voltages for maximum efficiency.
insights.locator: Monaka’s value proposition

insights.claim: Monaka implements a floating point register cache to help cache data in programs with high temporal locality, which describes a lot of GEMM workloads, plus predicate register bypass and masking of sub-256-bit vectors as zeros to cut SIMD power.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Micro-architectural power tricks aimed specifically at GEMM show Fujitsu targeting AI and HPC math rather than general server throughput.
insights.locator: Looking a bit more closely at power optimization techniques

insights.claim: Monaka's core die is built on TSMC's N2P while the SRAM and I/O dies use TSMC N5, with N2P covering less than 30% of total silicon area so most of the chip is on N5.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Confining leading-edge silicon to under 30% of area is a cost-control template that limits exposure to N2 wafer pricing and capacity.
insights.quote: N2P is used for less than 30% of the total silicon area; most of the chip is made on N5.
insights.locator: The core die is made on TSMC’s N2P process node

insights.claim: Splitting across nodes lets Fujitsu accelerate time-to-market for what is a cutting-edge chip.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Time-to-market, not just cost, is the argument for multi-node chiplets, which matters for how quickly Arm entrants can iterate against x86.
insights.quote: By splitting things up in this fashion, Fujitsu is able to accelerate their time-to-market for what is a cutting-edge chip.
insights.locator: The core die is made on TSMC’s N2P process node

insights.claim: The chiplet architecture uses die-to-die hybrid bonding with the core die sitting on top of the SRAM die and a silicon interposer below that.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Core-on-SRAM stacking is the same structural direction AMD and Intel are taking, confirming 3D cache stacking as the industry standard approach.
insights.locator: The chiplet architecture means using die-to-die hybrid bonding

insights.claim: 2nm will deliver a huge boost in chip density and performance thanks to GAAFETs, but it is not the optimal solution for all parts of a chip, which is why Fujitsu uses chiplets across multiple process nodes.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Reusable rule for reading any future chiplet design: leading-edge nodes go to logic, trailing nodes keep SRAM and I/O.
insights.quote: But it is not the optimal solution for all parts of a chip, which is why they are using chiplets built across multiple process nodes.
insights.locator: Looking a bit at the history of the semiconductor industry

insights.claim: Monaka is an Armv9.3-A design using 256-bit SVE2 SIMDs, a rarity in the Arm space where most designs use 128-bit SVE2, with dual SVE2 units and two 256-bit load/store units per core.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Wider SIMD than mainstream Arm server cores differentiates Monaka on vector throughput while avoiding A64FX's 512-bit overreach.
insights.quote: The chip uses 256-bit SVE2 SIMDs, which is a rarity in the Arm space as most designs have been 128-bit SVE2 (the exception being the 512-bit A64FX, of course).
insights.locator: Monaka is an Armv9.3-A architecture design

insights.claim: Monaka offers three NUMA configurations at 1, 4, and 8 nodes with 144, 36, and 18 cores respectively, where the 1-node configuration serves large memory applications and 8 nodes favor high throughput.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Configurable NUMA topology lets one part serve both large-memory and throughput tenants, useful for cloud operators consolidating fleets.
insights.locator: As for memory access and NUMA nodes

insights.claim: Monaka carries 12 channels of DDR5 memory, 144 CPU cores per chip, and can scale to 2P per node.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: 144 cores across 12 DDR5 channels places Monaka's memory-per-core ratio between Arm AGI and high-core-count x86 parts.
insights.locator: Monaka is an Armv9.3-A architecture design

insights.claim: Each NUMA node can be split into two LLC regions, and Monaka supports up to 63 MPAMs independent of the NUMA nodes.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Fine-grained resource partitioning is a multi-tenancy feature that matters for cloud providers selling isolated performance.
insights.locator: Each NUMA node can be split up into two LLC regions

insights.claim: Monaka will ship in two 144-core SKUs, a 500 Watt high-performance part with 2.9GHz base frequency and a 350 Watt high-efficiency part at 2.1GHz, with the high-performance SKU estimated at almost 50% higher performance.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: A 43% power increase buying 50% more performance sets the efficiency curve buyers must weigh against rack power constraints.
insights.quote: Both have 144 cores, but the high performance SKU will operate at 500 Watts, versus 350 Watts for the high-efficiency SKU. This brings the base frequency up from 2.1GHz to 2.9GHz, and an estimated performance of almost 50% higher.
insights.locator: Monaka will be offered in two SKUs

insights.claim: Fujitsu is positioning Monaka as a CPU built for modern AI workloads with far greater ambitions than the A64FX, which was primarily seen in the Fugaku supercomputer.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Signals Fujitsu attempting to convert a national-supercomputer program into a commercial server business, a much harder go-to-market.
insights.locator: While Fujitsu’s earlier A64FX CPU was primarily seen in the Fugaku supercomputer

insights.claim: Monaka is designed to meet the needs of sovereign AI alongside modern workloads and energy efficiency.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Sovereign AI procurement is a demand pool insulated from pure price-performance competition, favoring national champions like Fujitsu.
insights.quote: Monaka is designed to be a better fit for modern workloads, as well as meeting the needs of sovereign AI.
insights.locator: Monaka’s value proposition

insights.claim: The role of CPUs in AI systems is expanding because agentic workloads push CPUs far beyond just coordinating GPUs.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: A recurring Hot Chips 2026 theme: CPU attach value per AI rack is rising, not falling, which supports server CPU ASPs.
insights.quote: Agentic workloads are pushing CPUs like never before, as CPUs are doing far more than just coordinating GPUs these days.
insights.locator: According to Fujitsu, the role of CPUs in AI systems is expanding

insights.claim: Fujitsu makes heavy use of open source software for Monaka but is also tapping parts of NVIDIA's open source software stack to complete the ecosystem.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Even a sovereign-AI-positioned CPU depends on NVIDIA software, showing how deep that dependency runs across the industry.
insights.locator: And looking at the software ecosystem in a bit more detail

insights.claim: Monaka arrives in 2027 while Fujitsu is already developing Monaka-X, a faster chip fabbed on a 1.4nm process that will incorporate NVLink Fusion support for connectivity to NVIDIA and other NVLink accelerators.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: NVLink Fusion adoption by a third-party CPU vendor extends NVIDIA's fabric standard, a quiet but significant lock-in expansion.
insights.quote: Meanwhile the company is already in the process of developing Monaka-X, which will be a faster chip fabbed on a 1.4nm process, and which will incorporate NVLink Fusion support
insights.locator: Monaka is set to arrive in 2027

insights.claim: Confidential computing support is baked into Monaka as part of the Arm confidential compute architecture, requiring co-design between hardware, firmware, and the software stack.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Confidential computing is now a baseline requirement across every 2026-2027 server CPU disclosed, not a differentiator.
insights.locator: Confidential computing support is also baked into Monaka
